text:
margo: Heads up — after the OFED 5.10 rollout in euc2 earlier this morning we're seeing ~3–5x tail latency for large allreduce jobs. NCCL is frequently falling back to TCP on affected nodes.

infra-bot: deploy: OFED 5.10 rollout started euc2 at 08:12 UTC

sasha: Confirming. job-ml-904 had 4x slower median bandwidth, packets show retransmits. Anyone saw firmware or PCIe changes in the image?

leo: paste: dmesg on host node-32 shows IB warnings:
```
mlx5: mlx5_core 0000:6b:00.0: pcie link speed change detected: 8.0GT/s -> 5.0GT/s
mlx5_core: port 1: ecc errors increasing
ib_ipoib: device mlx5_0: port 1 down
```

margo: interesting — we didn't change NIC firmware in the OFED package but the new driver toggles ACS hardware arbitration. Could cause asymmetric pathing across PCIe root ports.

anita: @ryan FYI — did the onboarding script enable SR-IOV by default on the new AMIs? That + ACS could change VF routing.

ryan: We enabled SR-IOV for perf testing yesterday. I didn't expect ACS toggles. Reverting SR-IOV on a single host removed the pattern in my quick test.

sasha: How are we verifying fallback? Which metric showed TCP vs IB?

leo: `nvidia-smi topo -m` + `ibv_devinfo -v` showed missing GIDs on some hosts. Also saw the NCCL debug log with 'no p2p route, falling back to net'.

margo: workaround idea: pin NIC drivers to 5.9 and disable ACS on the kernel cmdline or via PCIe override in AMI. But that's heavy.

anita: For euc2 can we do a canary rollback of OFED 5.10 on a small subset and validate? We should also capture PCIe / lspci -vv and link_state before/after.

ryan: I'll schedule rollback on 3 nodes and run the allreduce microbenchmark. ETA 30m.

leo: Add check for asymmetric pathing to our node healthcheck: compare root port winners and link speeds; flag nodes with mixed link speeds.

margo: +1. Also add NCCL env logging to capture fallback reason. If this repeats we need vendor support (Mellanox) — collect full dmesg, ibstat, lspci, ethtool -S, and nv_peer_mem logs.

sasha: Thanks, team. I'll coordinate a sudden capacity plan if this hits more nodes — might need to shift jobs away from euc2 until canary validated. :eyes: 

infra-bot: incident: perf-degradation-euc2 created, severity=low, oncall=@sre-team
